title: Ring Oscillators
intro: A ring of an odd number of inverting stages has no stable DC state, so it oscillates.

blocks.text: With N inverting stages (N odd and at least 3) of delay Td each, the signal needs two trips around the ring (2N delays) to repeat:

blocks.alt: Three inverters connected in a loop. The output of each inverter feeds the input of the next, and the output of the third feeds back to the input of the first. A tap labelled out leaves the output of the third inverter.
blocks.caption: A three-stage ring oscillator.

items: More stages: lower frequency, lower phase noise per cycle but more power.
Delay depends on supply and temperature, so the ring is a VCO if the supply or bias current is varied.
Differential rings with delay cells are used in high-speed PLLs.

blocks.title: Ring frequency
blocks.text: Five stages, each with 20 ps delay. Find the oscillation frequency.

blocks.title: Why odd?
blocks.text: Why can an even number of inverters not oscillate?
solution: An even number of inversions gives positive feedback overall: two stable states (latch) exist. An odd number gives negative feedback with delay, and no consistent DC solution, so the signal keeps chasing itself.
